name: Teak Museum, Nilambur
tagline: Kerala’s teak heritage — museum, Conolly’s Plot and shaded forest walks
summary: World’s first thematic teak museum at the KFRI Nilambur sub-centre, beside historic Conolly’s Plot; museum exhibits, bio‑resources park and forest walks best enjoyed October–March.
description: The Teak Museum at Nilambur is a thematic, two‑storey museum on the Kerala Forest Research Institute (KFRI) sub‑centre campus that explores the history, science, cultivation and uses of teak. It was established in 1995 close to the historic Conolly’s Plot, the early 19th‑century teak plantation that made Nilambur famous. ([docs.kfri.res.in](https://docs.kfri.res.in/BNP/Teak-Musesum-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Visitors get a compact introduction to teak: displays include an exposed root system of an aged teak, classified teak poles, cultural objects (like model urus and granaries), and large ancient teak stumps that show the scale of old forests. Adjacent attractions on the campus include a bio‑resources nature park, butterfly/bamboo displays and interpretive forest trails. ([docs.kfri.res.in](https://docs.kfri.res.in/BNP/Teak-Musesum-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The museum pairs naturally with strolls through Nilambur’s shaded teak plantations such as Conolly’s Plot and nearby Nedumkayam reserved forest. These walks and the museum are particularly pleasant in the winter season (October–March) when temperatures are comfortable and the trails are dry. ([incredibleindia.gov.in](https://www.incredibleindia.gov.in/en/kerala/malappuram/neelambur-teak-forest?utm_source=openai))

This site matters because Nilambur helped shift local forestry from extraction to planned planting; the museum and the living plantation together tell that story while offering accessible forest experiences for families, students and nature travellers. Confirm details (opening times, guided‑walk bookings) with KFRI or local tourism before you travel. ([docs.kfri.res.in](https://docs.kfri.res.in/BNP/Teak-Musesum-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))
highlights: World’s first thematic teak museum (KFRI sub‑centre, est. 1995). ([docs.kfri.res.in](https://docs.kfri.res.in/BNP/Teak-Musesum-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Conolly’s Plot — the historic Nilambur teak plantation nearby. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/conollys-plot-nilambur-oldest-teak-plantation-2024/696/?utm_source=openai))
Bio‑resources Nature Park, butterfly and medicinal plant displays. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/teak-museum-nilambur/344/?utm_source=openai))
Shaded forest walks and educational trails ideal in winter (Oct–Mar). ([incredibleindia.gov.in](https://www.incredibleindia.gov.in/en/kerala/malappuram/neelambur-teak-forest?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: Background
body: Nilambur’s association with teak began in the 1840s when the British administration (H. V. Conolly and associates) initiated planned teak plantations; Conolly’s Plot near Nilambur remains an interpreted living plantation and a short walk from the museum. The museum itself was created by KFRI and the Kerala Forest Department to document the species’ history, management and uses. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/conollys-plot-nilambur-oldest-teak-plantation-2024/696/?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Browse the museum galleries to learn about teak biology, traditional uses, historic ship‑building and local craft; notable exhibits include an exposed 55‑year root mass display and large ancient teak stumps that show former forest giants. ([docs.kfri.res.in](https://docs.kfri.res.in/BNP/Teak-Musesum-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Take a short guided or self‑guided walk to Conolly’s Plot and the KFRI bio‑resources nature park to see mature teak stands, a bamboo grove and a medicinal plant garden; combine the museum visit with Nedumkayam rainforest trails if you have time. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/conollys-plot-nilambur-oldest-teak-plantation-2024/696/?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best time: October to March — cooler, drier weather makes museum touring and forest walks most enjoyable. Monsoon months (June–September) are lush but wet; summer can be warm in the middle of the day. ([incredibleindia.gov.in](https://www.incredibleindia.gov.in/en/kerala/malappuram/neelambur-teak-forest?utm_source=openai))

Facilities: the museum sits on the KFRI Nilambur campus and shares space with the bio‑resources park; modest visitor facilities are available but verify current opening hours and any guided‑walk schedules with KFRI or local tourism before you go. ([docs.kfri.res.in](https://docs.kfri.res.in/BNP/Teak-Musesum-en.pdf?utm_source=openai))

visitorInfo.howToReach: By train: Nilambur Road railway station (terminus of the Shoranur–Nilambur line), about 4–6 km from the museum; By air: Calicut (Kozhikode) / Calicut International Airport (CCJ) is the nearest major airport (roughly 50–55 km by road); By road: the museum is on the Nilambur–Gudalur (SH‑28) roadside, about 4 km from Nilambur town. ([incredibleindia.gov.in](https://www.incredibleindia.gov.in/en/kerala/malappuram/neelambur-teak-forest?utm_source=openai))
etiquette: Carry insect repellent and sturdy shoes for shaded plantation trails; some tracks are uneven after rain.
Morning visits are cooler and better for forest walks; combine the museum with a short visit to Conolly’s Plot and the bio‑resources park.

Guided forest walks or entry to some reserved areas may require booking or a permission — confirm with KFRI or the Kerala Forest Department before travel. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/teak-museum-nilambur/344/?utm_source=openai))
